standard.title: Evaluate identity shaped by language and culture
standard.description: reflect on and evaluate how their own and others' identify is shaped by language(s), culture(s), attitudes, beliefs and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can reflect on and explain how their own and others' identity is shaped by language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values (AC9LCH8EU04). They have examined cultural values in language use, reflected on identity across communities, and identified stereotyping risks. They have not yet evaluated how globalisation and cultural change affect identity, examined how language is used to empower or marginalise, or reflected on the academic and professional opportunities opened by bilingualism.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on and evaluate how their own and others' identity is shaped by language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values — including the impact of globalisation, power and marginalisation in language, and the opportunities created by bilingual identity.

nodes.label: Cultural change, globalisation and identity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how cultural traditions and globalisation affect identity and communication, and explain how cultural beliefs shape communication differences across Chinese-speaking communities.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate how at least two cultural traditions or globalisation-related changes have affected communication in the target language community, and explain the impact on own identity or beliefs.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate differences in perceptions, behaviours and communication across cultures; explain how cultural traditions and beliefs affect communication across regions; explore modesty, personal space and respect for authority in communication; reflect on how globalisation has affected own identity and beliefs.
wider: Research how a specific wave of globalisation has affected target language cultural practices and identity — evaluate whether the changes strengthen or challenge cultural continuity
Compare own intergenerational family experience of cultural change — identify what has been maintained, what has changed, and discuss the factors that drive cultural continuity or change
nodes.hinge_reason: Evaluating the impact of cultural change and globalisation on identity is the conceptual prerequisite for the most sophisticated identity analysis at this level. Students who can only describe cultural-language connections cannot evaluate the dynamic, contested relationship between language, culture and identity.

response_modes.reason: Evaluating cultural change requires students to reason about cause and effect, continuity and change, and competing values — a multi-step analytical process. Explicit frameworks for evaluating cultural impact build the critical analytical capacity the descriptor requires.

success_criteria: Evaluates how at least two cultural traditions or globalisation changes have affected communication
Explains the impact on own identity or beliefs with reasoned argument

nodes.label: Language, power and marginalisation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can examine how language may be used to empower or marginalise groups in society, and identify how access to sources and critical awareness can build mutual understanding.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two examples of how language is used to empower or marginalise in the target language community or across cultures, and explain the impact of each.
nodes.typical_width: Examine how language empowers or marginalises groups; identify content that creates bias or stereotypes; build mutual understanding through critical source evaluation; explore how group labels influence perception; examine how cultural assumptions are embedded in language; analyse gender language conventions.
wider: Conduct an analysis of a target language text or media source for embedded bias or marginalising language — identify specific language choices and explain how they position readers or particular groups
Compare how the same social group is labelled and discussed across target language and English media — identify differences in framing and discuss the cultural values that underlie each

response_modes.reason: Language and power analysis must be applied across varied contexts — media, group labels, gender conventions, community discourse — before students can generalise the critical framework. Varied examples build the analytical lens that transfers across new texts and contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students often have direct experience of how language shapes belonging and marginalisation across cultural contexts. Width investment here connects this lived experience to critical analytical frameworks — building the intellectual capacity to understand and articulate what has been personally experienced.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two examples of language used to empower or marginalise
Explains the impact of each with specific reference to language choices

nodes.label: Bilingual identity and world view expansion
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how their bilingual identity opens opportunities to expand world views and pursue heritage and cultural connections, reflecting on the academic and personal significance of language knowledge.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate at least two ways in which bilingual identity opens opportunities — academic, professional, cultural, or personal — and reflect on at least one heritage or cultural connection made possible by target language knowledge.
nodes.typical_width: Identify how knowledge of target language and English opens opportunities; read texts across languages to expand perspectives; analyse own language and cultural background through family conversations; discover own heritage through target language; evaluate the personal significance of bilingual identity.
wider: Produce a sustained reflective evaluation of own bilingual identity journey — tracing how it has developed, what has shaped it, and its significance for future study, community connection and professional aspiration
Interview a family member or community member about the opportunities their bilingualism has created — compare their experience with own and discuss what has changed across generations

response_modes.reason: Bilingual identity evaluation integrates cultural change analysis (node 1) and power/marginalisation awareness (node 2) into a personally grounded synthesis. The teaching investment is in creating genuinely reflective conditions — space for honest, complex identity examination rather than tidy resolution — where students can articulate what their bilingual identity means to them.

success_criteria: Evaluates at least two ways bilingual identity opens opportunities
Reflects on at least one heritage or cultural connection made possible by target language knowledge
